column3: Ok
column4: The command did what was asked.

column3: Failed
column4: The command ran and failed — the pre-existing catch-all, and still where every failure that has not been deliberately classified lands (see `From<String> for CliError`).

column3: Usage
column4: The command line was wrong: an unknown verb, an unknown flag, a missing required flag, a bad value.

column3: Connect
column4: A service could not be reached: no datahub, no node, a refused or timed-out connection.

column3: Refused
column4: Refused LOCALLY — by a ceiling, a client-side guardrail, a book selector naming an account a READ has no row field to check against (`crates/vike-cli/src/cmd/trade/selector.rs`'s `refuse_an_unaddressable_book`, its first live producer), or a capability the connected node does not advertise — which is how a risk-reducing verb naming a book (a mass-cancel, flatten or close-all) is refused today — before anything was sent in every case.

column3: Venue
column4: The venue or the node accepted the request and REJECTED it: the far side spoke, and it said no.

column3: Breach
column4: A DECLARED THRESHOLD WAS BREACHED — the product of this crate's JUDGING verbs, one per plane (`vike-cli backtest gate`, `vike-cli data history gate` and `vike-cli strategy sdk-diff`, whose threshold is "the two SDKs' results are identical"), and the one rung on this ladder that is a RESULT rather than a failure.

column3: Empty
column4: NOTHING WAS EVALUATED — an empty slice, no coverage, zero trials, a run directory with no report in it, or a set of criteria that named no key the document carries.

column3: OutcomeUnknown
column4: The OUTCOME IS UNKNOWN — a write was sent and no verdict came back, so it may or may not have happened: read the book before resending it.

column3: compute a strategy over history and judge what came back: `backtest run` runs one on a remote backtesthub — `vike-backend backtesthub --addr`, config.backtest_addr — or --local, and the PROFILE says what — a [paramscan] grid searches the parameter space, a [walkforward] table walks it forward, and declaring both ships the profile whole to the walk-forward runner. Then `backtest ls|show|path` over the run directory, `tag` to name a run, `diff` to see what moved between two, `gate` to turn that into a CI exit code, and `params` and `strategies` for what can be tuned and what can be run. Before a strategy exists: `templates` ships starters, `script-api` prints everything a Rhai script may call, and `script-check` compiles one and answers in the exit code. `prune --dry-run` lists the saved runs config.saved_runs_per_strategy would remove

market data, every verb under a REQUIRED group: `data history` is a past window in the hist store — fetch, import or load the published real bars into it (no demo or synthetic tape ships), read and export what it holds, report coverage and gaps (over --addr); `realtime` is now (watch, status, record), `catalog` what is addressable, `source` where rows may come from, and `instruments` and `splits` the operator's own rows

this box's settings: provenance (`show`), a validating pre-flight (`check`) and journalled one-key changes (`set`, `unset`), plus the stored rows a deploy builds and an operator edits — the profiles this box runs from, a symbol rename, the instruments the operator added, the venue address rows (`url`) and the IBKR cash-settled futures roots; `config --help` lists every verb

observe + control a running vike-tradehub: the NODE-WIDE words take no group — `trade status|health|links` read the node and `trade halt|resume` set its trading mode — and the rest live under a REQUIRED group: one account, its orders, positions and strategies, its venue's own reads, and the reconcile divergences held for an operator (`trade --help` lists them; `watch` is named and refused as designed-not-built); a bare `trade` opens the interactive REPL (for a human)

the results of a run on this machine (`report run:@last`) or of a live account read from the datahub (`report account:binance/MAIN`), two side by side with `--compare`; read-only — the live-journal `--node` and a bare run selector are retired and refused, naming the spelling that replaced each

investigate a signal and FIT a model — the plane BEFORE a strategy exists: `research study` asks the backtesthub (`vike-backend backtesthub --addr`, config.backtest_addr) to run a study FILE over the hist store it holds; a peer that does not advertise `study` (the data server, an older backtesthub) is refused by name and pointed at `vike-backend study`

what a strategy FILE does across the numbered SDKs it can be built against: `strategy sdk-diff` runs one backtest with the file built against SDK N and against SDK M on the backtesthub and compares every metric, the trades and every recorded field (exit 0 identical, 6 they differ, 7 neither traded so nothing was compared, 1 a run or a build failed); `--all` reports a folder, a line a file. `strategy migrate` first rewrites a Rust file's JSON `save_state`/`load_state` onto `StrategyState` (ABI 15), pinned or not, and a bar's or a tick's `String` symbol onto `vike_marketdata::Symbol` unless its pinned SDK already lends `Symbol` rows (a hook or read of another shape gets a hint and is left as it is), then moves a file pinned to `sdk = N` to a newer SDK one SDK at a time, each step built before it is kept, or applies the renamed names to a Rhai script; the original is kept as a numbered backup, and `--dry-run` writes nothing
